name: Sickle Cell Disease
description: Sickle cell disease is a group of inherited red blood cell disorders in which red blood cells become hard and sticky and look like a C-shaped farm tool called a sickle. These cells die early, causing a constant shortage of red blood cells and can block blood flow causing severe pain and other complications.
prevalence: 1 in 365 African American births; 1 in 16,300 Hispanic American births
ageOfOnset: Typically diagnosed at birth through newborn screening
prognosis: Significantly improved with modern treatment; many patients live into their 50s-60s

patientOrganizations.name: Sickle Cell Disease Association of America

eli5Summary: Sickle cell disease makes red blood cells change shape from round to curved like a banana. These oddly-shaped cells get stuck in blood vessels and don't carry oxygen well, causing pain and other problems. New gene therapies can now fix the problem at its source.
clinicalSummary: Sickle cell disease results from homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the HBB gene, causing production of hemoglobin S (HbS). Polymerization of deoxygenated HbS causes erythrocyte sickling, leading to hemolytic anemia and vaso-occlusion. Major complications include acute pain crises, acute chest syndrome, stroke, and progressive organ damage. The 2023 FDA approval of two gene therapies (Casgevy using CRISPR-Cas9 and Lyfgenia using lentiviral gene addition) represents a paradigm shift toward functional cure.
historicalBackground: Sickle cell disease was the first molecular disease characterized, with Linus Pauling identifying the abnormal hemoglobin in 1949. The specific mutation (Glu6Val) was identified in 1956. The 2023 approval of CRISPR-based Casgevy marked the first CRISPR gene therapy approved in the US, representing a historic milestone in medicine.

recentBreakthroughs.title: BMJ roadmap for scaling gene therapy across Africa
recentBreakthroughs.description: BMJ Global Health published "Beyond hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: positioning Africa for scalable uptake of innovative sickle cell therapies" on 25 May 2026, setting out infrastructure, regulatory and financing requirements for delivering curative therapies where disease burden is highest.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Mitapivat sickle cell application gets FDA priority review
recentBreakthroughs.description: On 7 July 2026 the FDA granted priority review to Agios' supplemental NDA for mitapivat (Pyrukynd) in sickle cell disease under the accelerated approval pathway, with a PDUFA goal date of 1 November 2026, based on the 207-patient RISE UP phase 3 trial.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Etavopivat meets both co-primary endpoints in phase 3
recentBreakthroughs.description: Novo Nordisk reported on 20 April 2026 that oral etavopivat in the 385-patient HIBISCUS trial cut annualised vaso-occlusive crises by 27% versus placebo and produced a >1 g/dL haemoglobin rise at 24 weeks in 48.7% versus 7.2% on placebo; filing was planned for H2 2026.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Two CRISPR editing trials published together in NEJM
recentBreakthroughs.description: The New England Journal of Medicine published in April 2026 "Base Editing of HBG1 and HBG2 Promoters for Sickle Cell Disease" (BEAM-101) and "CRISPR-Cas12a Gene Editing of HBG1 and HBG2 Promoters to Treat Sickle Cell Disease" (reni-cel) — the first peer-reviewed clinical results for next-generation fetal-haemoglobin-reactivating editing platforms.

recentBreakthroughs.title: EMA confirms continued EU suspension of Oxbryta
recentBreakthroughs.description: In October 2025 the EMA's CHMP confirmed that Oxbryta (voxelotor) remains suspended in the EU, concluding that benefits no longer outweigh risks after excess deaths and vaso-occlusive crises in HOPE Kids 2 and RESOLVE, with no subgroup identified in which benefit outweighed risk.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Real-world gene therapy outcomes
recentBreakthroughs.description: Early real-world data shows sustained disease resolution in patients treated with gene therapy.

recentBreakthroughs.title: First CRISPR gene therapy approved
recentBreakthroughs.description: FDA approves Casgevy (exa-cel), the first CRISPR-based therapy, offering potential cure for sickle cell disease.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Second gene therapy approved
recentBreakthroughs.description: Lyfgenia (lovo-cel) approved as alternative gene therapy approach using lentiviral vector.
